newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil's Norne field delayed - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Statoil's Norne field delayed - newspaper.

text.p: Development of the Norne oilfield in the Norwegian Sea is delayed by about one month and will run at least 150 million crowns over budget, the daily Stavanger Aftenblad said on Friday.
Norne, operated by Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil), is being developed via production ship and a system of subsea wells. It was originally planned to come on stream in July.
"According to plans the ship should have left the Aker Stord yard in April and started production in July," the newspaper said.
"Now production director Kjell Helle has confirmed to Aftenblad that the ship will stay at the yard until May and that first oil will be delayed until August."
Helle said the number of hours of work required on the vessel at Stord had double from 200,000 to 400,000, which had pushed costs up by around 150 million crowns.
Aftenblad said Helle blamed the extra time on the Far East Levingstone Shipbuilding (Feis) yard in Singapore.
"Statoil is not pleased with the way Feis has performed this job. We have found large mistakes and seen a lot of bad workmanship," Helle told the daily.
But the newspaper added that according to the original plan for production and operation compiled in 1994, Norne was scheduled to start up in December and cost around 9.8 billion crowns.
"Now the field will start in August, while the price is down to 7.3 to 7.5 billion crowns," Stavanger Aftenblad said.
Statoil was not immediately available for comment.
